full_judgment: 2. The petitioners as plaintiff filed the Title Suit No. 34 of 1985 for declaration of title in the suit land stating, inter alia, that one Govinda Chandra Chakraborty was the superior landlord in Mirashi right in 'A' schedule land and while the same was under his management one Bhama Baishnabi was given shelter in the suit land by the said Govinda and CS record was recorded in the name of the said Bhama Baishnabi. About 60 years ago the said Bhama Baishnabi died leaving one heir and thereafter said Govinda, superior landlord of the Estate, took the 'A' schedule land in his khas possession. In the "B" schedule land said Govinda Chandra was owner in possession as Mirashi right, Govinda died leaving only two sons namely, Mukunda and Gopal. By an amicable settlement between these two brothers Mukunda got the suit land. Mukunda in exercising his sixteen annas right, title and interest in the suit properties approached to plaintifs father for taking settlement of the suit properties on payment of reasonable rent for the suit land and thereafter Mukunda gave rioyti settlement by executing an unregistered Hukum Nama with respect to the suit properties in the Bengali year 1343 BS on 17th Poush corresponding to 1936 in favour of Krishna Mohan Das, the father of the plaintiffs. Krishna Mohan Das was owner in possession of the suit properties by getting settlement and he died in the year 1956 at his own house in the suit Mouza leaving behind three sons, the plaintiffs who by inheritance became the owner and possessed the entire suit land for more than 12 years uninterruptedly and have been paying rent to the Government and that on 17-8-85 for the first time they came to know from the local Tahsilder that the suit properties have been treated as vested properties by the defendants No. 5 and 6 as the properties were earlier recorded in favour of defendant Nos. 1-4 and also Tahsilder refused to accept the rent from the plaintiffs. The defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit properties and SA Khatian has been wrongly prepared in faovur of the defendant Nos. 1-4 due to such recording in favour of the defendant No. 1-4 a cloud of doubt in the right, title and interest of the plaintiff in the suit land and to dispel such cloud and doubt plaintiffs have constrained to file the suit.
